question: Does supervised adaptation on the chronological first 20% of each held-out session materially improve continuous ECG on its disjoint final 80%?
protocol_label: subject-calibrated few-shot; not strict zero-shot LOSO
split: MMECG loso_v2 development validation folds 1/5/9; test unopened
calibration: per record, windows ending at or before 20% of record duration
query: same record, windows starting at or after the 20% boundary; no source-sample overlap with calibration
initialization: source-trained fold-matched calibration-guided REM full-arm checkpoint
adaptation: adapter parameters only; frozen B1 backbone; exactly 100 AdamW steps at lr=1e-4 on calibration windows; no query-based early stopping or selection
primary_metric: full-window query PCC, per window then fold aggregated
gate: on fold 1, adapted REM exceeds conventional PCC by >=0.05 and source-trained REM by >=0.03 without worsening RMSE or R2
test_policy: validation only; test files remain unopened
